title: Password Security & Management Policy Template
metaDescription: Comprehensive password policy template with strong password requirements, two-factor authentication guidelines, and security best practices.
description: Create a robust password security policy for your organization with this comprehensive template. Includes password strength requirements, two-factor authentication protocols, password manager guidelines, and breach response procedures.

sections.heading: Policy Overview and Purpose
sections.content: This Password Security and Management Policy establishes mandatory requirements for creating, managing, and protecting passwords across [ORGANIZATION_NAME]. This policy aims to safeguard sensitive information, prevent unauthorized access, and maintain the integrity of our digital systems. All employees, contractors, and authorized users must comply with these password security standards to protect against cyber threats, data breaches, and identity theft.

sections.heading: Password Creation Requirements
sections.content: All passwords must meet the following minimum requirements: 1) Minimum 12 characters in length, with 14+ characters strongly recommended. 2) Must include at least three of the following: uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters (!@#$%^&*). 3) Cannot contain dictionary words, personal information (names, birthdates), or common patterns (123456, qwerty). 4) Must be unique across all systems and accounts. 5) Cannot reuse the last 12 passwords. Use a password generator tool or secure browser like Incognito Browser to create strong, random passwords that meet these criteria.

sections.heading: Password Manager Implementation
sections.content: [ORGANIZATION_NAME] requires the use of approved password managers for all work-related accounts. Recommended password managers include [APPROVED_PASSWORD_MANAGERS]. Password managers must: 1) Use strong master passwords following the same requirements outlined above. 2) Enable automatic password generation for new accounts. 3) Store all work-related credentials securely. 4) Sync across authorized devices only. 5) Be configured with automatic logout after [TIMEOUT_PERIOD] minutes of inactivity. Personal password managers may be used for work purposes if they meet our security standards and are approved by IT.

sections.heading: Two-Factor Authentication Requirements
sections.content: Two-factor authentication (2FA) is mandatory for all business-critical systems, including: email accounts, cloud storage services, financial systems, administrative panels, and remote access tools. Acceptable 2FA methods include: 1) Authenticator apps (Google Authenticator, Authy, Microsoft Authenticator). 2) Hardware security keys (YubiKey, Titan Security Key). 3) SMS verification (only when other methods unavailable). 4) Biometric authentication on approved devices. SMS-based 2FA should be avoided when possible due to SIM-swapping risks. All 2FA backup codes must be stored securely in your password manager.

sections.heading: Password Change and Rotation Policy
sections.content: Regular password updates are required under the following circumstances: 1) Immediately upon suspected compromise or security incident. 2) When leaving the organization or changing roles. 3) Every [ROTATION_PERIOD] days for high-privilege accounts. 4) After any system security breach affecting the account. 5) When sharing violations are discovered. Standard user passwords should be changed immediately if compromised but do not require routine rotation if they are strong and unique. Focus on password strength over frequent changes to avoid user fatigue and weak password creation.

sections.heading: Prohibited Password Practices
sections.content: The following password practices are strictly prohibited: 1) Sharing passwords with colleagues, family, or third parties. 2) Writing passwords on paper, sticky notes, or unsecured digital documents. 3) Using the same password across multiple accounts. 4) Storing passwords in browsers without master password protection. 5) Sending passwords via email, text message, or unsecured communication channels. 6) Using public computers or networks for password-protected accounts without proper security measures (use Incognito Browser or private browsing mode). 7) Saving passwords on shared or public devices. Violations may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination.

sections.heading: Account Security Monitoring
sections.content: All users must actively monitor their accounts for suspicious activity: 1) Enable login notifications and security alerts for all business accounts. 2) Regularly review account access logs and authorized devices. 3) Report suspicious login attempts or unauthorized access immediately to [IT_CONTACT]. 4) Monitor credit reports and financial accounts for signs of identity theft. 5) Use breach monitoring services to check if accounts have been compromised in data breaches. 6) Implement account lockout policies after [FAILED_ATTEMPTS] failed login attempts. Regular security awareness training will be provided to help identify and respond to threats.

sections.heading: Incident Response and Breach Procedures
sections.content: In the event of a suspected password compromise or security breach: 1) Immediately change the compromised password and any shared passwords. 2) Report the incident to [INCIDENT_CONTACT] within [REPORT_TIMEFRAME] hours. 3) Document the incident including timeline, affected accounts, and potential impact. 4) Enable additional security monitoring on affected accounts. 5) Review and revoke unnecessary account permissions. 6) Conduct a security assessment to prevent future incidents. 7) Notify affected parties and stakeholders as required by law and company policy. All incidents will be investigated and may result in additional security training or policy updates.

useCases: Developing IT security policies for businesses
Establishing incident response procedures for password breaches
